title: Risk: identifying, quantifying and planning a response

videos.script: Imagine it is six months from now, and the project has failed. Write down why. {{premortem}} That question, asked of the Agenda team, produced five risks in twenty minutes, including one nobody had said aloud: only one developer understands billing. {{five}} This lesson turns that list into numbers. Probability times impact gives each risk an expected cost in days. {{numbers}} The four threats add up to nine days, and that is a reserve you can explain to a sponsor, risk by risk. {{reserve}} Then it chooses a response for each one: avoid, transfer, mitigate or accept. {{responses}} And it ends with the risks an architect is best placed to find: the new technology, the integration nobody controls, the decision that cannot be undone. {{technical}}
